message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Typical Value (STP) | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Symbol** | H | From Latin *hydro* “water”. |
| **Isotopes** | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) | Deuterium is stable; tritium is radioactive (half‑life ~12.3 yr). |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | Weighted average of isotopes. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Moderately high for a metal‑free element. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | Energy to remove the single valence electron. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV | Small negative value (tends to lose rather than gain an electron). |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; boils at ~20 K. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies at ~14 K. |
| **Density (liquid)** | 0.0708 g cm⁻³ | Very low; less dense than air. |
| **Molecular weight** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ (H₂) | Diatomic gas under normal conditions. |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | Strong covalent bond. |
| **Flammability range** | 4–75 % (v/v) in air | Highly combustible; forms explosive mixtures. |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals | Forms H₂O, HF, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| **Solubility in water** | 0.0007 g g⁻¹ (at 25 °C) | Poorly soluble; tends to escape from aqueous solutions. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible) | Classic hydrogen emission spectrum. |
| **Uses** | Fuel cells, rocket propellant, ammonia synthesis, hydrogenation reactions | Central to many industrial processes. |

### Quick Highlights

- **Lightest element** – lowest mass per atom and per molecule.  
- **Most abundant element in the Universe** – ~75 % of baryonic mass.  
- **Highly reactive** – readily forms bonds with almost all other elements.  
- **Key role in life** – essential component of water, organic molecules, and metabolic pathways.  
- **Energy carrier** – clean combustion produces only water vapor; used in fuel cells for electricity generation.  

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property!
